title: Pizza Quattro Stagioni
subtitle: Four-seasons pizza with artichokes, mushrooms, ham, and olives
excerpt: Pizza Quattro Stagioni divides the disc into four sections, each with a different topping: artichoke hearts, mushrooms, cooked ham, and black olives. The sections share tomato and mozzarella as a base. It is a composed pizza rather than a jumble, and the division is part of how it looks as much as how it tastes.
sourceNotes: Pizza Quattro Stagioni (four seasons) is a classic Italian pizza found across Rome and Naples. The division of the pizza into four sections representing the four seasons is an established format, though the specific toppings for each quarter vary by region and restaurant.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the dough 24 hours ahead. Drain and prepare all toppings before you start shaping the discs.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan or conventional, maximum oven setting. Preheat with a heavy tray or pizza stone for at least 45 minutes.

content.text: Pizza Quattro Stagioni is a tomato and mozzarella pizza divided into four quadrants, each with its own topping. The sections are artichoke hearts, sauteed mushrooms, sliced cooked ham, and black olives. You get a bit of each in every few bites. The challenge is laying out the sections clearly before the pizza goes in the oven, because once it bakes they become harder to distinguish.
You need one 210 g ball of 24-hour pizza dough per pizza, rested at room temperature for 2 hours before shaping.

items.prepNote: sliced and sauteed in olive oil until golden
or cooked ham, torn into pieces

content.text: Heat the oven to its maximum setting with a heavy tray or pizza stone on the top shelf. Preheat for at least 45 minutes.
Fry the sliced mushrooms in a little olive oil over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes until golden and any moisture has cooked off. Season with salt and set aside.
Season the passata with salt. Drain and halve the artichoke hearts.
Stretch one dough ball to a rough 30 cm disc. Spread the passata over the base and scatter mozzarella over the whole disc.
Divide the pizza mentally into four quarters. Arrange the artichoke hearts in one quarter, the mushrooms in a second, the ham in a third, and the olives in the fourth. Drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the rim is charred and the mozzarella is bubbling. Eat immediately.

The four-seasons pizza is found in both Naples and Rome, with different interpretations. The Neapolitan version tends to use jarred artichokes, mushrooms, tomato, mozzarella, and black olives. The Roman version sometimes includes capers. The consistent element is the visual division of the disc, which makes the pizza easy to share by section.
